question_text: If an online store can’t ship my order by the promised date, can it just delay the order without asking me?
answer_text: No. If it cannot ship on time, it generally must get your consent to the delay or promptly refund your money.
attestation_text: Source: Federal Trade Commission — FTC, Business Guide to the Mail, Internet, or Telephone Order Merchandise Rule, delayed shipment requirements

question_text: For a credit card, how long before the due date must the bill generally be sent or delivered?
answer_text: The bill generally must be mailed or delivered at least 14 days before the payment due date.
attestation_text: Source: Consumer Financial Protection Bureau — CFPB Ask CFPB, How long before my credit card payment due date does the card issuer have to mail or deliver my bill?

question_text: When substituting dried herbs for fresh herbs in a recipe, what ratio should I use?
answer_text: Use about 1 teaspoon of dried herbs for each 1 tablespoon of fresh herbs.

question_text: Which Great Lake has the greatest maximum depth?
answer_text: Lake Michigan has the greatest maximum depth, at about 1,332 feet.

question_text: If I take money out of a traditional IRA before age 59½ and no exception applies, what extra federal tax usually applies?
answer_text: The extra federal tax is generally 10% of the taxable part of the early distribution.
attestation_text: Source: Internal Revenue Service — IRS Publication 590-B, Distributions from Individual Retirement Arrangements (IRAs), section on additional tax on early distributions

question_text: What is the maximum total acetaminophen an adult should take in one day from all medicines combined?
answer_text: The adult maximum is 5,000 mg in 24 hours from all acetaminophen-containing medicines.

question_text: If I enroll late in Medicare Part B and don’t qualify for a Special Enrollment Period, how is the late enrollment penalty usually figured?
answer_text: It is usually 10% for each full 12-month period you could have had Part B but did not, and it usually lasts as long as you have Part B.

question_text: If the IRS mails me a notice of deficiency, how long do I generally have to file a petition with the U.S. Tax Court?
answer_text: You generally have 120 days from the notice date to file a Tax Court petition, or 180 days if the notice is addressed outside the United States.
